user_saw: Some messages in a long Discord reply sent with Windows-style line endings ended with a stray carriage return.
summary: The Discord chunker now drops the whole CRLF separator at a message boundary and preserves the pair inside inline code.
reasoning: The July 1 snapshot already split on LF alone and emitted the accumulated text verbatim, so a flush at a CRLF line boundary could leave a bare CR. The September Unicode patch explicitly preserved that cut. Offline path history stopped at the shallow boundary, so I could not establish which earlier commit introduced the behavior.
